zero_omission_notes.summary: Explains core market mechanisms: Law of Demand (inverse price-quantity relation), Law of Supply (direct price-quantity relation), market equilibrium where demand equals supply, and government price regulations (price ceilings and price floors).

detailed_sections.full_notes: Other things remaining constant (ceteris paribus), as price increases, quantity demanded decreases; as price decreases, quantity demanded increases. Demand curves slope downward from left to right due to income and substitution effects.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ceteris Paribus
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Latin phrase meaning 'all other factors remaining equal' (consumer income, tastes, related good prices remain constant).

detailed_sections.full_notes: Other things remaining constant, as price increases, quantity supplied by producers increases; as price decreases, quantity supplied decreases. Supply curves slope upward from left to right driven by profit motivation.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Profit Incentive
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Higher market prices increase profit margins, incentivizing suppliers to expand production output.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Market Equilibrium occurs where Quantity Demanded = Quantity Supplied at Equilibrium Price (Pe). If Price > Pe: Excess Supply (Surplus) forces price down. If Price < Pe: Excess Demand (Shortage) pushes price up. Price Ceiling (max price below Pe) creates shortages; Price Floor (min price above Pe, e.g. MSP) creates surpluses.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Price Ceiling vs Price Floor
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Price Ceiling: Maximum legal price charged (protects consumers, e.g. essential drugs). Price Floor: Minimum legal price (protects producers, e.g. Minimum Support Price for farmers).

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Plotting Demand and Supply Curves to Find Market Equilibrium - Graphically determine equilibrium price and quantity from market schedule data.
procedure_or_steps: Plot Price (Rs) on vertical Y-axis and Quantity (Units) on horizontal X-axis.
Plot downward-sloping Demand Curve (D) from schedule points.
Plot upward-sloping Supply Curve (S) on same graph.
Identify intersection point (E) where D and S cross.
Read corresponding Equilibrium Price (Pe) and Quantity (Qe).
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: The intersection point explicitly pinpoints the exact price where buyers and sellers agree.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Market prices automatically adjust toward equilibrium via competitive buyer-seller interaction.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.figure_id_and_title: Fig 9.1: Market Equilibrium, Shortage, and Surplus
diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw intersecting D and S curves. Mark horizontal price lines above Pe (Surplus) and below Pe (Shortage).
diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Price above Pe causes Qs > Qd (Surplus); Price below Pe causes Qd > Qs (Shortage).

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A state where market demand equals market supply, establishing a stable clearing price with no excess shortage or surplus.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: At Rs. 40/kg, the quantity of apples buyers want equals the quantity sellers supply.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A legally imposed maximum price that sellers can charge for a good or service, set below equilibrium price.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Government sets a price ceiling on essential medicines to keep them affordable.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.si_unit_or_notation: Q_d: Quantity Demanded; Q_s: Quantity Supplied; P: Market Price.

textbook_exercises.question: Explain what happens when government sets a price ceiling on milk below equilibrium price.
textbook_exercises.answer: Setting a price ceiling below equilibrium price lowers milk price for consumers. However, at this lower price, quantity demanded increases while dairy suppliers reduce quantity supplied. This creates a persistent market shortage (Excess Demand), leading to long queues, rationing, or black markets.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: According to the Law of Demand, what happens when the price of a normal good falls, assuming ceteris paribus?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: The Law of Demand states an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded.

short_answer_questions.question: Differentiate between a Price Ceiling and a Price Floor.
short_answer_questions.answer: 1) Price Ceiling: Legal maximum price set BELOW equilibrium price to protect consumers (causes shortage). 2) Price Floor: Legal minimum price set ABOVE equilibrium price to protect producers/farmers (causes surplus). Key points: Max vs Min price distinction, Placement relative to equilibrium price, Shortage vs Surplus outcome

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Source Passage (Price floor is an imposed limit on how low a price can be ch...): Give a real-world example of an effective price floor in India.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Minimum Support Price (MSP) for agricultural crops set by the Indian government to protect farmers against price crashes.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Using a demand and supply diagram, explain how market forces automatically restore equilibrium when price is set above equilibrium price.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: 1) When price (P1) is above equilibrium price (Pe), Quantity Supplied (Qs) exceeds Quantity Demanded (Qd), creating Excess Supply (Surplus). 2) Sellers find unsold inventories accumulating in warehouses. 3) To clear unsold stock, competing sellers lower their prices. 4) As price falls toward Pe, quantity demanded expands along the demand curve while quantity supplied contracts along the supply curve. 5) Price reductions continue until Qs = Qd at equilibrium price Pe, eliminating the surplus.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A sudden severe drought destroys 40% of the onion crop nationwide before the winter harvest season.

qa.question: Analyze the impact on the onion market supply curve, equilibrium price, and quantity.
qa.answer: The crop destruction causes the onion Supply Curve to shift leftward. At the original price, excess demand occurs, driving the new equilibrium price significantly upward while reducing equilibrium quantity.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Confusing a 'change in quantity demanded' with a 'change in demand'.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: 'Change in quantity demanded' is a movement along the same demand curve caused solely by a price change; 'Change in demand' is a shift of the entire curve caused by non-price factors (income, tastes).
